forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Corporate Costs & Provisions has not yet actioned spend towards Local Government Re-organisation, and the forecast shows no variance for it.
findings.detail: The paper says the announcement on Local Government Re-organisation and its impact have not been reflected in this cost area at the time of writing. Corporate Costs & Provisions is forecast on budget, with an underspend to date of £361,811.
findings.matters: Local government reorganisation costs are a live question for councils across England, and this paper shows the cost area still awaiting the announcement's impact.
findings.figures: Approved budget £2,738,260; budget to date £1,924,990; actual to date £1,563,179; variance to date (361,811); forecast variance 0
findings.quote: The spend to date has not actioned spend towards Local Government Re-organisation.

findings.headline: Legal Services is forecast £50,000 over budget for defence and appeals work, which the paper describes as estimated and to be monitored through the year.
findings.detail: The forecast is £50,000 above budget, based on legal fees for defence and appeals work. The paper states the figure is an estimate that will be monitored during the year.
findings.matters: Defence and appeals legal costs are often hard to forecast, and the paper flags the estimate as subject to in-year monitoring.
findings.figures: Approved budget £603,600; forecast £653,600; forecast variance £50,000; variance to date £32,311
findings.quote: Legal Fees for various defence and appeals work. Forecast reflects higher than budgeted.

findings.headline: Crematorium and Cemeteries is forecast £229,622 over budget, with cremation fee income behind plan and £48k of unbudgeted cremator maintenance.
findings.detail: The paper says cremation fee income (standard charge) is behind plan and that cremator maintenance costs were not budgeted for, at £48k. The forecast reflects both effects against a budget of £(1,132,600).
findings.matters: Cremation income and cremator maintenance are a recurring issue for councils running crematoria, and an unbudgeted £48k of maintenance is a specific figure another finance team can test.
findings.figures: Budget £(1,132,600); forecast £(902,978); forecast variance £229,622; unbudgeted cremator maintenance £48k
findings.quote: Cremation fees (standard charge) income is behind plan. Cremator maintenance costs unbudgeted for, £48k.

findings.headline: Leisure and Culture is forecast £244,320 above budget, with income from leisure revised down by £178k.
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast for culture services income was revised downwards along with an increase in staff costs to ensure service cover. Community Centres and Community and Sports Development are forecast to finish favourable, partly offsetting the overall position.
findings.matters: A leisure income shortfall that is partly offset by staff cost increases is a pattern other councils running leisure services will recognise.
findings.figures: Leisure and Culture line: budget £1,471,070; forecast £1,725,909; forecast variance £254,839. Leisure and Culture total forecast variance £244,320. Income from leisure revised by £178k.
findings.quote: Culture services income forecast revised downwards along with an increase of staff costs to ensure service cover.

findings.headline: King's Lynn & West Norfolk car parking income is forecast at £3,283,963 against a £2,880,200 budget, a forecast variance of £403,763 favourable.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the additional income above budget partly to a dry summer. Carparking Shared Services is shown on budget, with the paper noting its spend to date does not yet include overheads and recharges.
findings.matters: Car parking income depends on weather and footfall, and the paper ties part of a large forecast over-recovery to a single season.
findings.figures: Approved budget £(2,880,200); forecast £(3,283,963); forecast variance £(403,763); variance to date £(31,978)
findings.quote: Additional income above budget, dry summer has aided this.
